title: The UNTOLD Story Of India's UNICORN - Meesho | Sanjeev Barnwal | FO 38 - Raj Shamani
text: Japanese are very punctual.We had to enter the office by 9:25 am. If it becomes 9:30, I lose my half day. The exact problem that you're solving right now, today, you should keep your ego aside. For the first 2 years we did not think about skale. I've had the fortunate to spending 20 minutes with Richard Branson and I talked about absolute bullshit. You were one of the 1st companies to get funding from Facebook. -Yeah. Yeah. And how did that happen? Tell me one thing, I was reading about your journey and I found out I dunno if that's true or no, you have to tell me. You guys left the job in starting, that now we will only do startup. -Yeah. You didn't know what startup to do?How to do it? You just had to do it. Is this right? It's perfectly right. I think and to some.. You dropped out.Like I mean.. I'll give some background.What happened was Oh... so I was in Sony with in Japan for 3 years. As a software developer, building Sony mobiles. I thought that in life what is next 10 years going to look like? What next 20 years is going to look like?Maybe. And I thought that maybe we should create something which has massive impact. And this is me thinking, myself alone,like this 1 year before leaving Sony. So I thought okay let's try something and I found a couple of colleagues in Sony. So Sony are getting Indians from same college. There's someone junior,one junior one senior. We started working on some project. Some random hobby project trying to create a product out of it. Did not work out. Fast forward 1 year. It hasn't worked out. I'm still thinking what do I do next. And then one startup from Bangalore approached me saying that do you want to join us? I called with it that seems like these guys are interested. I think how is how is Bangalore doing and.. basically we're very good friends in college. Okay. -But what happens is after college you stay connected on Whatsapp group. So our wing mates 8 to 10 people connected on our Whatsapp group. A lot of chitchat happening everywhere.Just don't call. Calling is too much friction. But they call that man tell me what is happening and he said that let's start-up and the kind of trust that we had because of the 4 years that we spent together in college, we were good friends, did lot of projects together, played lot of call of duty together. It was the the favorite. -Typical engineering behavior. We played a lot of games I think. But then when did the actual idea came in? Because so I'll tell you this is you know your journey is fascinating and different because I have I have this notion that now people become entrepreneur by choice. Earlier people used to become entrepreneurs out of adiversity or out of lack of options. -Yeah. Right. That I have a problem which is disturbing so they would want to do it. Or did not get any other option, did not get a job somewhere or did not get support financially so they did it. Right. Now, people have good job ,stability and evrything but now they're like no man enough is enough now we want to do start-up or do something different. So if you ask any founders that should people do it? Everybody's like oh there should be a problem, it needs to be solved.So till the problem is not found, one should not leave the job, should not do it. And your journey has been different. -Correct. Like if you want to do start-up, then we'll figure it out. No I think they're the..I agree I think when we were trying to, we decided that yes let's do it. We read about a lot of these things and thought that man no one is doing anything like people find out ideas and then leave jobs. Like with me what happened was because I had tried for a year, something right, something else for a year and did not workout while as in Sony. I thought that it wont happen like this. You need to get in full time. And if you want to really find out properly you'll have to spend a lot of time in a particular domain and it doesn't necessarily have to be your problem. -Yeah.  So if you put the limitation of just exploiting problem that you are facing directly, there might not be enough problem. There might not be big enough problems. So we thought that what will happen? We'll just take a plan and we'll figure it out but doesn't workout, we'll go back to our jobs. So it's not that risky anymore. So let's if someone who wants to start up right now, okay. And they want to start up because Let's do it now, what are the next 10 years looking like in life?  We'll make a start-up. Right and because of that if people want to come up with an idea and they want to find problems is that any framework which you follow? Like oh these are the things which, 2 or 3 things which  we should, which you should care of to come up with ideas. What happens, is there such a frame work? -Right. No I think when we left the job and started creating excel sheet. Hmm.. Okay. What are the ideas that we can potentially pursue? Few things that.. and not everything was perfect then like we were not aware of everything but looking back few things that you should definitely keep in mind is 1. How big that problem is?Right. Umm... The market size of the problem, if you are able to solve it while the market size keeps changing. Over time while trade you you change etc. But broadly when you try to solve a problem,how big the problem is?That is important,so I think the many should have a problem. It's important because it's a long commitment to spend maybe at least 10 years if you want to build something really successful. Maybe 5-10 years or even more. So you should pursue something, it for me personally and for us personally for me and Vidith personally it was like we want to pursue something  huge. Because 10 years is a lot of life. Yeah. And that is one, second do you have the right expertise to solve that problem? Right for example if you're trying to solve a problem around space technology,right. You need that expertise. Because if you don't have that expertise you better prepare for it, you better go ahead.. How do people prepare for it let's say you didn't have an expertise of building something like e-commerce, you were a developer with it does is he an expert in the industry,no right. You both were like newbies. -Ecommerce is easier to me. So I think non- deep tech heavy domains are still easier. I think developing and understanding in a non- deep tech heavy domain is not that difficult. Whether it is e-commerce or any kind of marketplace. There's standard fundamentals of a how do you run marketplace, standard problems. You do need a techie because you want to build something you wanna build a tech business so you need a good techie and Me and Vidith were taking care of the entire tech. He was taking care of non-tech. So expertise gap was not there but when I say expertise it's not about having an expertise in the domain but it's about whatever required to go ahead and solve the problem in that, can you acquire that skill very quickly? But say space technology for example it is very different because you now have to Let's say non-deep tech heavy, let's say e-commerce. And do you have the ability to acquire certain skills where today may be it's e-commerce tomorrow you have to pivot into for example, like helping these people with finance so in Fintech or maybe educate these people your seller and some  next to Edtech. So you need to be very skillful in order to acquire new skills on everyday basis, right. So -Right. can you give an example that okay this is what is needed for this x. So you can learn it like this. Got it. So yeah I'll give you an example. So let's say for us ecommerce itself right. So when we started we wanted to figure out how do you acquired your first 1000 users. We wanted to figured out how to crack this zero to one stick? This is not that difficult,right.There are only maybe 10 or 20 ways of approaching users in early stages,right. And there's no group marketing witnesses. So example in our case what happened was umm.. so we started something called Fashnear which was fashion nearby not Meesho. Which was more like -What did you start with? Fashnear, fashion in nearby which was essentially a hyperlocal fashion marketplace from Bangalore itself,Koramangala and HSR. Now which was just mapping the offline fashion shops on the app and people had option of ordering by sitting at home. Multiple problems with that model and that is where we booted but yeah. Now when you want to reach out to first 100 users. Like what do you do? Now, how do you reach out to a specific set of 100 users in and around Koramangala and HSR? I think an easier way to do that is just give some kind of flyer inside newspaper. So I did it and we went to that newspaper distribution center that we have Forum mall somewhere there. And at Forum mall you just convince someone that man please can you take some money and put it inside. It's not that difficult skill like we hadn't done it ever but figuring out how to get like first 100 users and that will be very different from let's say when you start growth marketing then you need to understand how to do digital marketing. Like, what are the fundamentals of running good Facebook ads good Google ads. There are a lot of courses out there. You can always go and learn them.You'll learn the fundamentals.Everything else is applying those fundamentals to your own business context. So these kind of problems are not very difficult or these kind of skills are not very difficult to acquire. Versus let's say if you want to build rockets. You want to build more efficient rockets. You need to go deeper,spend maybe multiple years just to understand how rocket technology works.So these are two extreme examples but Basically,just trying to fit your skill sets. -I get it but you know both have a problem.Let's say deep tech, lets avoid that for a while because that need a specific expertise,right. Which is non-deep tech. Like ecommerce,so the first 100 users can be acquired. I'm sure the way you approached, there are 100 such other ways that people know that it is very easy but they're not doing it  because they feel that if I start in such place, then will I be doing this work? Like it's so small. Meaning it is so small that my job would have been better than this. it's not big enough. So many people, they start looking at ideas and because the ideas are so small that's why they never pursue it. So I think these are two different things. Ideas should be big,potential of that idea should be really big. The exact problem that you're solving right now today, you should keep your ego aside. So you just cannot always expect the odd rule to be just solving interesting problems always, like for us when we launched Fashnear I think there was one thing like newspaper distribution second was going to people in malls giving out flyers, convincing them. I was doing coding. I used to, I like programming. I was enjoying my job and if I am standing outside a mall and is not in my comfort zone,like I haven't done this ever so but I go and talk to a stranger was coming out of mall and asking them madam do you want to try out Fashnear and giving a flyer. I think first 10 conversation will be very difficult. Next 10 will be easier. You just have to keep that growth mindset mode on. But keeping your ego aside because you'll always out of these 10 you'll get another 5 who are just going to tell you man don't approach me. -Hmm.. I'm not interested and you'll feel bad about it you'll feel dejected but, but I think keeping your ego aside is extremely important. Without that it's not possible. -So the potential of the idea should be very big enough. And that will be the motivating factor probably that is north star like you keep that in mind always.The smaller problems in the near future over a shotter period, doesn't matter. -Yeah true but then you should keep doing things which are which matter on a day to day basis. Which are... which probably would require you to do stuff where your ego will come in between and you have to give that aside,right. In fact I have.. like I used to say this when I build my startup and when I build my business and in that business when people say, what really worked for me.So I used to say that, you know, doing things which are non-scalable -Yeah. was my advantage. So Why would you say that? I'll tell you like in the beginning everybody is thinking about scale,is thinking about growing at large,right. And people who are let's say,if I'm operating for example, Unilever,okay,I'm operating in Fmcg space. -Yeah. So if I'm upgrading in Fmcg the space then if I do something that is easily scalable then Unilever would come.If it works Unilever will come and destroy me. -Correct. So I need to do something that is non- scalable which is very easy but it's very.. means he can't do it with a 100 people. Let's say, example would be, every time somebody buys from me I would give them a personalized note. Yeah. That ex-buyer bought this so personalizing according to him and care deep enough. I wrote a note for them and give it to them. I know that more than 20 notes a day,I can't do it. -Yeah Right. But that, that will become advantage because no other company is doing that with the customer. So that customer will feel a attached to me. And these 20 customers a day, let's say 200 in 10 days will become my hardcore fans. And Unilever wouln't have those 200 fans. Those 200 fans initially will become my advantage. Once I have 200, I will get some money then I can start something which is scalable. Correct. Basically, yes so equivalent of this exists and our business as well like and what we're trying to do is you find that one small group of users who no matter what kind of mess you end up doing, like they're still loyal to you. In some form or the other. So it'll be, they'll be using the product no matter what kind of issues are there. That is your core tg that you're talking about. Your first 100 users who really love your products so much that they'll keep complaining about your product that your loading time is too long,your app doesn't load and there are bugs but they'll keep using it. So they'll keep giving you feedback and they'll keep using it. And agreed,those are the users which you really need to find because that is your testing round. Yeah. -That is when you learn a lot. And I think for us that has been the case always like In fact in the first 2 years or rather this current model of Meesho started in 2017. Hardly 2017. For the first 2 years we did not think about scale. It was more about... First 2 years you didn't think about scale? It was more about writing crappy could just to make sure you're out there trying to test out your hypothesis. So because you're doing, if you do 10 things maybe 1 will work out. Yeah. But if you start solving each and every problem that's, assuming scale will.. assume scale as a problem in mind for each of these time.You're wasting so much time. Yeah. So what do you end up doing and the right thing to do for us was You just keep iterating very quickly,you don't care about code quality,don't care about X tax. Only thing you care about is, your first priority is solving the problem for the users. Getting your hypothesis out very quickly. Second is, okay, if you have time then focus on let's say, if it comes down to scaling,do you have the foundation right or not? You have the right architecture or not? And then could be something else. But in the beginning itself you start thinking about building scalable systems for you, you generally end up spending lot more time than required. So while you were working there, you were there for 3 years, rught so, did you notice any differences between Japanese working culture or India was there primary difference but you were like swayed away? This is a very cool thing, why is it not in India? No I agree I think, so the things which I liked and the things which I did not like and do not replicate.. -So tell me one thing that you did not like or didn't replicate and things which like a lot. Yeah I think the thing which I liked a lot and I did try to replicate is that they are very organized. Japanese. -Very organized, I think organized on the way they think about problems, the way they run projects, the way they keep track of progress ground projects,the way they collaborate with each other. They run a very tight ship. They are very organized to have a defined process for each and every thing. They're very well known in the world for processes. -Exactly. Six sigma etc came from their end. But yeah, there have been..they've done that really well,very organized and to some extent when we were growing while of course, process is seen as a anti- culture to some extent. Those people hate,  people in startups hate  processes but I think I believe that there is right amount of process for every startup at a given stage.Yeah so I think then I took a lot of motivation in handling the projects and yeah, that is something that I really liked. What was something you didn't like? -Yeah,I think they have a lot of.. Like,what happens in Japan,I won't be doing it in India. Yeah I think it's still, it's a phenomenal culture difference. It's the way we think about time. I think the Japanese are very punctual. Extremely punctual and I'll give you one example. Umm.. So we had to report, we had to enter the office by 9:25am. And tap it. And if it becomes 9:30am, I lose my half day. If I repeat the same thing for the 7 to 10 times, I start losing my one day leaves. -Oh.. So it is that strict like 1 minute of delay is not tolerable. And Trains there run within 1 minute of delay, 1 or 2 minutes of daily. And if a train is late by let's say,3 or 4 minutes you'll get a mini/small peice of paper which essentially a certificate issued from the station and other Metro trains, you get a certificate issued by the station that this train was delayed by 5 minutes, Which you can go in a apply in the HR portal and justify why I was 3 minutes. That punctual. And I think culturally we are different. We're not wired to be that punctual also if you want to be,there a lot of problems right.Infrastructure is not really predictable,like if I leave, if I want to cover 1 kilometer in Banglore, it would take anywhere between 5 to 10 minutes and I didn't want to apply that,yeah... It's not the right thing to do. So not that punctuality to that extent. Punctuality is expected not mandatory. Exactly,punctuality is expected -Okay now there's another interesting fact which I was reading about you guys was a that you were one of the first companies to get funding from Facebook. -Yeah. Yeah. And how did that happen?Like,did you go to Facebook and knock their doors that bro you know we exist give us the money. or they reached out to you hey you know what, I think you guys are doing something great we would want to fund you.How did you? How did the entire process happen?Like, how to get fund from Facebook? And I think well,I was not involved in this directly because Vidith leads the fundraising discussions but as far as I know and I remember I think Facebook knew that, so social commerce even now and even at that point of time in India happens on Facebook and whatsapp those are the two primary,wned by Facebook group or Meta. And I think they knew that social commerce is going to be really big, it solves lot of problems and new style of... new way of doing e-commerce, focus on below the belt cities so I think they would have already known at some point that it's going to be big. So probably they would have already been on lookout on which are the next bigger companies which can.. which, with whom they can partner to kind of get some benefits out of it and maybe help their own users, leverage social commerce. So probably I think we got connected to Facebook through some connections but it was not that they were one sided,they knew everything about it. Ohh.. -So it was Like you were already doing good work which.. they had an idea on I think matrix solves a lot of problems like if you, and we have been going crazily I think the last 3 years we have 100 or something is what the number that I saw it's difficult to remeber the exact numbers 3 years back roughly this is the number I saw floating somewhere in the tunnels,right. Okay so when you say that,when you keep seeing social commerce, okay. How is it different than e-commerce? Like I mean I get it it's a part of it but... I think e-commerce, so if you go... See there's a website so I go to the website and list something and millions of people come and buy them. That's direct ecommerce, right. Now what is social commerce? -Social commerce is essentially Internet commerce which, where social connections play an important role. Okay. -So social connections enabling you to drive that purchase. -As in like I didn't get it. Social connection means? So let's say one form of social commerce is.. are entrepreneurs themselves which is, entrepreneurs are connected to their own customers. So they're using social connection to drive that purchase, to drive that commerce. So in some form or the other leveraging your own social network to either drive purchase directly or build confidence as well. Which is it's not just about the last step which is just driving the budget but also about building conviction that this is the right product for me. Some kind of ocial validation maybe. So I think over time we have seen the lines between commerce and social media getting blurred. Which is people.. ohh... wow want to spend a lot of time in let's say, discovering new trends. At the same time it happens on Instagram, we have a community inside Meesho app as well where we see this happening also where people engage with each other but also try to get validation that one different kind of product. Like it's just really good... So technically how I mean to say so I'd say we all have this one person have in our inner family or we know relative that man if you want to buy an Ac, talk to him, he knows everything. So that person instead of talking to him that person can essentially built a.. like a catalog on your app or on your platform and then instead of he recommending it,they can say that check this, I have seen these 3-4, it is very good, you have bought it. -And that is social validation. Again a part of social commerce. I think social commece is a broad term for social validation being one of them,second would be direct driving the direct purchase. Again multiple problems, so then we stumbled upon the core problem again by staying closer IUS which was biggest problem for them,for these entrepreneurs was finding newer products to sell on a constant basis. We have always been very transparent with our thinking. And that pays off really well but we build the second app. After that we saw our matrixs get off through the roof, doubling every month, for the next 4-5 months, we raise our CDC's after that. No I think we should think about tech as a nice tool to have in your skillset to solve every problem in a more efficient way.
